Borrower's failure to make such deposit shall constitute an Event of Default.

### 7.6 Change Orders

Borrower shall not approve or permit (a) any change order, amendment or modification to the Construction Contract, (b) any change in the plans and specifications, or (c) any increase in the Renovation Budget, in any such case that individually or in the aggregate exceeds One Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($100,000.00), or that reduces the scope of the work in any material respect, without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower may approve change orders not exceeding such threshold in the aggregate, provided that (i) such change orders do not reduce the scope of the renovation in any material respect, (ii) no Event of Default exists, and (iii) Borrower delivers copies of all such change orders to Lender within ten (10) Business Days. In no event shall any change order be funded from the Renovation Holdback unless it increases the Renovation Budget and Lender has approved the funding source.

### 7.7 Inspection

Lender and its agents, representatives, architects, engineers and third-party inspectors may enter upon the Property at reasonable times and upon reasonable prior notice (or at any time without notice following an Event of Default) to inspect the progress and quality of the renovation, the workmanship and materials, and Borrower's compliance with this Article 7. Borrower shall cooperate with all such inspections and shall cause the Contractor to do so. The cost of any such inspection shall be borne by Borrower as provided in Section 22.9.

### 7.8 Failure to Complete; Lender's Right to Complete

If Borrower fails to commence or diligently pursue the renovation, or fails to complete the renovation by the Substantial Completion Deadline, or if an Event of Default occurs and is continuing, Lender may (but shall have no obligation to), in addition to all other remedies available under the Loan Documents, (a) withhold further disbursements from the Renovation Holdback, (b) enter upon the Property and take such actions as Lender deems necessary to complete or protect the renovation, (c) engage the Contractor or another contractor to complete the work, and (d) apply all remaining amounts in the Renovation Holdback Account and any other Reserve Account to the costs thereof. All amounts so expended by Lender shall constitute advances under Section 9.14 and shall be secured by this Mortgage. Lender's exercise of any right under this Section 7.8 shall not cure any Event of Default, shall not constitute an assumption of any obligation of Borrower and shall not create any liability of Lender to Borrower, Guarantor, the Contractor or any other Person.

### 7.9 Bay 1 Slab and Land Use Restriction Coordination

Borrower shall not permit any renovation, construction, demolition or alteration activity that penetrates, removes, compromises or otherwise affects the vapor barrier installed beneath the concrete floor slab of Bay 1 (Lot 7, ground floor) unless (a) Borrower has given prior written notice to SCDHEC as required by the LUR, (b) Borrower has obtained Lender's prior written consent, which consent may be conditioned upon delivery of an environmental consultant's written plan for inspection, repair or replacement of the vapor barrier, and (c) the work is performed in a manner that preserves or restores the integrity of the vapor barrier in compliance with the LUR. Borrower shall deliver to Lender copies of all correspondence with SCDHEC relating to the LUR and all vapor barrier inspection reports within five (5) Business Days after the same are sent or received. Borrower acknowledges that the façade restoration, HVAC replacement and elevator modernization comprising the Renovation Budget may require work in proximity to the Bay 1 slab and agrees to conduct such work in accordance with this Section 7.9.

### 7.10 Permits and Board of Architectural Review Approval

Borrower shall obtain and maintain all permits, licenses and approvals necessary for the renovation, including without limitation approval of the façade restoration (including the decorative iron balcony) by the City of Charleston Board of Architectural Review, in each case prior to the commencement of the affected work. Borrower shall promptly deliver copies of all such permits and approvals to Lender and shall comply with all conditions thereof.

## ARTICLE 8 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

Borrower represents and warrants to Lender, as of the Closing Date and as of each date on which any advance is made under the Loan Documents, as follows:

### 8.1 Organization; Authority

Borrower is a limited liability company duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of South Carolina, is duly qualified to do business in each jurisdiction in which the nature of its business or the ownership of the Property requires such qualification, and has all requisite power and authority to own the Property, to carry on its business as presently conducted and as contemplated by the Loan Documents, and to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under the Loan Documents.

### 8.2 Enforceability; No Conflicts

The execution, delivery and performance by Borrower of the Loan Documents have been duly authorized by all necessary limited liability company action, including by Graydon Development Group LLC as Managing Member and by the Members to the extent required by the Operating Agreement, and do not and will not (a) violate the articles of organization, the Operating Agreement or any other organizational document of Borrower, (b) violate any applicable law, order, judgment or decree, (c) result in a breach of or default under any indenture, agreement or instrument to which Borrower is a party, including without limitation the Leases and the Construction Contract, or (d) require any consent or approval of any Person that has not been obtained. The Loan Documents constitute the legal, valid and binding obligations of Borrower, enforceable against Borrower in accordance with their terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium and similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and to general principles of equity.

### 8.3 Title; Permitted Exceptions

Borrower has good, marketable and insurable fee simple title to the Property, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, and this Mortgage constitutes a valid first-priority lien on and security interest in the Property, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions. The Title Commitment accurately reflects all matters of record affecting the Property, and there are no unrecorded leases (other than as disclosed in the rent roll delivered to Lender), options, rights of first refusal, contracts of sale or other interests in the Property other than as disclosed in the rent roll and the Permitted Exceptions.

### 8.4 Leases; Rent Roll

The rent roll dated as of the Closing Date delivered to Lender and attached as Exhibit D is true, correct and complete in all material respects and accurately describes each Lease affecting the Property, including the premises, term, rent, escalations, security deposits, renewal options, rights of first refusal, termination rights, exclusives and assignment and subletting provisions. There are no Leases affecting the Property other than those described in Exhibit D and the matters described in Exhibit B. Borrower has delivered to Lender true, correct and complete copies of all Leases, together with all amendments, side letters and guaranties relating thereto. No tenant is in material default under its Lease, no tenant has asserted any material claim, offset, defense or setoff against Borrower, and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time or both, would constitute a material default by Borrower under any Lease.

### 8.5 Environmental

Except as disclosed in the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Report No. CLR-2025-0119 dated January 28, 2025 prepared by Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC (the "**Phase I Report**") and in Exhibit E, (a) to Borrower's knowledge, the Property is free of Hazardous Materials and has not been used for the generation, treatment, storage, disposal or release of Hazardous Materials; (b) Borrower has not received any notice of violation of or liability under any Environmental Laws relating to the Property; (c) the Property is in compliance with the LUR and all applicable Environmental Laws; (d) the vapor barrier beneath the floor slab of Bay 1 is intact and has not been penetrated, removed or compromised; and (e) there are no pending or, to Borrower's knowledge, threatened claims, actions or proceedings relating to the environmental condition of the Property. Borrower has delivered to Lender a true and complete copy of the Phase I Report and has obtained for Lender the reliance rights of an intended user thereunder.

### 8.6 Single-Purpose Entity

Borrower is, and since its formation has been, a single-purpose entity that owns no assets other than the Property and the Collateral contemplated by the Loan Documents, has incurred no indebtedness other than the Loan and trade payables incurred in the ordinary course of business, and has conducted no business other than the ownership, operation, renovation, leasing and management of the Property. From and after the Closing Date, the Operating Agreement shall contain the single-purpose entity provisions, separateness covenants, Independent Manager requirement and other restrictions required by Article 14, and all Members shall have executed the Operating Agreement Amendment.

### 8.7 Litigation

There is no action, suit, proceeding, arbitration or governmental investigation pending or, to Borrower's knowledge, threatened against Borrower, Guarantor or the Property that, if adversely determined, would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect or that questions the validity of any Loan Document.

### 8.8 Insurance

Borrower has obtained, and shall maintain, all insurance required by Article 11, and each such policy is in full force and effect, with premiums paid current, and names Lender as mortgagee, loss payee and/or additional insured, as applicable.

### 8.9 Financial Statements

The financial statements of Borrower and Guarantor delivered to Lender are complete and correct in all material respects, have been prepared in accordance with GAAP consistently applied (subject, in the case of interim statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes), and fairly present the financial condition and results of operations of Borrower and Guarantor as of the dates and for the periods indicated. There has been no Material Adverse Effect since the dates of such financial statements as delivered.

### 8.10 No Defaults; No Subordinate Financing

No Event of Default or event that, with notice or lapse of time or both, would constitute an Event of Default exists under the Loan Documents. Borrower has no subordinate or mezzanine financing, preferred equity or other indebtedness secured by the Property or any direct or indirect interest in Borrower, and has granted no lien on or security interest in any Collateral other than the Permitted Exceptions.

### 8.11 Zoning; Permits; Compliance with Laws

The Property is zoned GB (General Business) under the zoning ordinance of the City of Charleston, and the current and contemplated use of the Property complies with such zoning. All permits, certificates of occupancy, licenses and approvals required for the current use and occupancy of the Property and for the renovation have been obtained or will be obtained in accordance with Section 7.10. Borrower is in compliance with all applicable laws, ordinances, codes, orders and regulations relating to the Property and its business, including without limitation all zoning, building, fire, health, safety, accessibility and Environmental Laws.

### 8.12 Construction Contract

The Construction Contract is in full force and effect and has not been amended, and no default exists thereunder by Borrower or, to Borrower's knowledge, by the Contractor. The Contractor holds all licenses, permits and insurance required for the renovation, including South Carolina General Contractor License No. SC-GC-47921.

### 8.13 Taxes

All real property taxes, assessments and governmental charges affecting the Property for all periods prior to the current year have been paid in full, and no delinquent taxes, tax liens or pending tax sales exist with respect to the Property.

### 8.14 Survival

The representations and warranties set forth in this Article 8 shall survive the Closing Date, the making of the Loan and any foreclosure, sale or transfer of the Property, and shall be deemed remade as of the date of each advance under the Loan Documents.

## ARTICLE 9 — AFFIRMATIVE COVENANTS

Borrower covenants and agrees with Lender that, from the Closing Date and until the Obligations have been paid and performed in full, Borrower shall:

### 9.1 Payment and Performance

Pay and perform, when due, all of the Obligations and all of its obligations under the Loan Documents and the Leases, and maintain the Property in compliance with all covenants, conditions and restrictions affecting the Property, including the Permitted Exceptions, the LUR, the Leases and the Construction Contract.

### 9.2 Maintenance and Repairs

Maintain the Property, including all Improvements, fixtures, building systems, common areas, landscaping, parking areas and the vacated Anson Lane strip, in good order, condition and repair, consistent with the standards of comparable mixed-use commercial properties in the Charleston, South Carolina metropolitan area, and promptly make all repairs, renewals, replacements and restorations necessary to preserve the value and utility of the Property. Borrower shall not commit or permit any waste of the Property or any portion thereof, and shall not remove, demolish or alter any Improvement except in connection with the renovation or as permitted by Section 10.7.

### 9.3 Compliance with Laws

Comply at all times with all applicable federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations, orders, ordinances and governmental requirements applicable to the Property and the conduct of Borrower's business, including without limitation all zoning, building, fire, health, safety, accessibility and Environmental Laws, and all covenants, conditions and restrictions of record affecting the Property. Borrower shall not use or permit the use of the Property for any purpose that would violate any such requirement, any Permitted Exception or any Lease, and shall not permit the Property to be used for any residential purpose on the ground floor of Lot 7.

### 9.4 Taxes and Assessments

Pay and discharge before delinquency all real property taxes, assessments, water and sewer charges, license fees and other governmental charges imposed upon the Property or upon the Obligations, except to the extent such amounts are being paid from the Tax and Insurance Escrow Account or are being contested by Borrower in good faith by appropriate proceedings diligently conducted, provided that Borrower has furnished such security as Lender may reasonably require. Borrower shall deliver to Lender copies of all tax bills and notices of assessment within ten (10) days after receipt and shall notify Lender of any pending or proposed tax reassessment or appeal affecting the Property.

### 9.5 Insurance

Maintain at all times the insurance required by Article 11, with financially sound and reputable insurers acceptable to Lender, and deliver to Lender the certificates of insurance, endorsements and other evidence required by Article 11.

### 9.6 Leasing Covenant

Use commercially reasonable efforts to lease all vacant space at the Property (including Bay 2 and 2nd Floor Suite B) at market rents, on terms consistent with those prevailing for comparable mixed-use commercial properties in the Charleston, South Carolina metropolitan area, and on terms reasonably acceptable to Lender. All new Leases, and all modifications, extensions and renewals of existing Leases, for premises in excess of five thousand (5,000) square feet or for terms exceeding five (5) years (including any renewal or extension option) shall require Lender's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Borrower shall not enter into any Lease that (a) violates, or would permit the violation of, the LUR, (b) violates any exclusive use or right of first refusal granted to an existing tenant, including the exclusive use granted to Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as specialty grocery and the right of first refusal granted to Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC with respect to Bay 2, (c) provides for rent payable more than one (1) month in advance, or (d) contains any option to purchase, right of first refusal to purchase or right of first offer to purchase the Property or any portion thereof. Borrower shall deliver to Lender a copy of each proposed Lease and such credit and other information as Lender may reasonably request at least ten (10) Business Days prior to execution of any Lease requiring Lender's consent.

### 9.7 Estoppel Certificates and SNDAs

Deliver to Lender, within fifteen (15) days after Lender's written request, estoppel certificates and, where requested by Lender, subordination, non-disturbance and attornment agreements from each tenant under the Leases, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Lender, and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain from each tenant under the Leases such further consents to the assignment of Leases and Rents as Lender may reasonably request. Borrower shall promptly notify Lender of any request for estoppel received from any actual or prospective mortgagee or purchaser of the Property and shall respond to such request within the time required by the applicable Lease.

### 9.8 Financial Reporting

Deliver to Lender the financial statements, rent rolls, operating statements, leases and other reports required by Section 13.3, in each case in the form and within the time periods specified therein.

### 9.9 Financial Covenants

Maintain compliance at all times with the financial covenants set forth in Article 13.

### 9.10 Books and Records; Inspection

Keep adequate books of account and records in accordance with GAAP, and permit Lender and its agents, accountants and representatives to examine, audit and make copies of such books and records and to inspect the Property at reasonable times and upon reasonable prior notice.

### 9.11 Further Assurances

Execute, acknowledge, deliver, file, record and re-record such further instruments and take such further actions as Lender may reasonably request to carry out the purposes of the Loan Documents, including without limitation the Operating Agreement Amendment, UCC continuation statements, title affidavits, gap indemnities, consents to assignment, subordination agreements and zoning reports.

### 9.12 Appraisals

Permit Lender, at Borrower's expense, to obtain an appraisal or appraisal update of the Property (a) at any time after the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, and (b) otherwise no more frequently than once in any twelve (12) month period, or more frequently if required by applicable law or regulation. Borrower shall cooperate with any appraiser retained by Lender and shall provide access to the Property and all information reasonably requested.

### 9.13 Notice of Certain Events

Promptly notify Lender in writing (and in any event within five (5) Business Days) of (a) any Event of Default or any event that, with notice or lapse of time or both, would constitute an Event of Default, (b) any material default by any tenant under a Lease or any tenant bankruptcy, insolvency or vacating of premises, (c) any litigation, arbitration or governmental proceeding affecting the Property, Borrower or Guarantor that would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect, (d) any casualty, condemnation, violation notice, lien, encumbrance or tax reassessment affecting the Property, (e) any notice, order or communication from SCDHEC or any other governmental authority relating to the LUR or the environmental condition of the Property, (f) any change in the identity of any Member, the Managing Member, the general partner of any Member, or any manager or officer of Borrower, and (g) any change in Borrower's name, state of organization, organizational identification number, Federal Employer Identification Number, principal place of business or registered agent.

### 9.14 Advances by Lender

Pay to Lender on demand all amounts expended by Lender pursuant to this Mortgage, the other Loan Documents or applicable law, including without limitation amounts paid for taxes, insurance, repairs, maintenance, environmental remediation, completion of the renovation, liens, inspections, appraisals and enforcement costs, together with interest thereon at the Default Rate from the date of expenditure until repaid. All such amounts shall constitute advances secured by this Mortgage, and Lender's payment thereof shall not cure any default or waive any right of Lender.

### 9.15 Protection of Lender's Interest

Take all actions necessary to preserve and protect the lien of this Mortgage, the Assignment of Leases and Rents and Lender's security interests in the Collateral, including the filing and continuation of financing statements, the payment of recording and filing fees, and the defense of any claim that would impair Lender's interest.

### 9.16 Registered Agent; Good Standing

Maintain its existence and good standing in the State of South Carolina and in each other jurisdiction in which qualification is required, and maintain a registered agent for service of process in the State of South Carolina.

## ARTICLE 10 — NEGATIVE COVENANTS

Borrower covenants and agrees with Lender that, from the Closing Date and until the Obligations have been paid and performed in full, Borrower shall not, without Lender's prior written consent:

### 10.1 No Subordinate Financing

Incur, create, assume, permit to exist or suffer any lien, mortgage, deed of trust, security interest, pledge, encumbrance, charge or other financing arrangement secured by the Property or any portion thereof or by any direct or indirect interest in Borrower, or any subordinate, mezzanine, preferred equity or other indebtedness of Borrower, whether secured or unsecured. This Section 10.1 applies to all forms of indebtedness and financing arrangements, including mezzanine loans, preferred equity interests, ground leases, sale-leaseback transactions, synthetic leases and any other arrangement that may affect Lender's collateral position or priority.

### 10.2 Transfer Restrictions

(a) Sell, convey, transfer, assign, pledge, mortgage, encumber or otherwise dispose of the Property or any portion thereof or any interest therein, or any interest in the Collateral.

(b) Permit any transfer of direct or indirect ownership interests in Borrower, or any change of control of Borrower or of any Member that constitutes a Controlling Member, except that the following transfers (collectively, "**Permitted Transfers**") shall be permitted without Lender's consent, provided that no Event of Default exists and Borrower gives Lender at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice:

(i) a transfer of direct membership interests in Borrower that does not exceed ten percent (10%) individually or twenty-five percent (25%) in the aggregate (measured cumulatively from the Closing Date) and that does not result in any Person or group of Persons acquiring control of Borrower;

(ii) a transfer by a Member that is a passive investor holding less than twenty percent (20%) of the membership interests in Borrower to an Affiliate of such Member, provided that the transferee executes a joinder to the Operating Agreement and the Members' Consent and remains subject to the restrictions of Article 14; and

(iii) a transfer of direct membership interests among the existing Members occurring after the date hereof that does not (A) increase the aggregate direct or indirect interest of Graydon Development Group LLC and Guarantor in Borrower above seventy-two percent (72%), (B) reduce the direct or indirect interest of Graydon Development Group LLC in Borrower below fifty-one percent (51%), (C) result in any Person other than Graydon Development Group LLC serving as Managing Member, or (D) otherwise result in a change of control of Borrower.

(c) Permit any change of control of any Member that is a Controlling Member, including without limitation any transfer of the direct or indirect ownership interests in Graydon Development Group LLC, any change in the identity of the general partner of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, any transfer of membership interests in Borrower to a "successor fund" or similar vehicle under Section 4.2(c) of the Operating Agreement, or any merger, consolidation or reorganization of any Member, in each case without Lender's prior written consent.

(d) For purposes of this Section 10.2, "**Controlling Member**" means Graydon Development Group LLC and any other Member that, together with its Affiliates, holds directly or indirectly fifty percent (50%) or more of the membership interests in Borrower or has the right to designate the Managing Member, and "**control**" has the meaning given to such term in the Operating Agreement.

(e) Any transfer in violation of this Section 10.2 shall be void ab initio, shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 16.1(k) without any notice or cure period, and shall entitle Lender to accelerate the Obligations, to impose the Default Rate and to exercise all other remedies under the Loan Documents and applicable law.

(f) Borrower acknowledges that (i) Section 4.1 of the Operating Agreement restricts transfers of membership interests but does not address changes in the internal or upstream ownership, management or control of any Member, and (ii) Section 4.2(c) of the Operating Agreement permits transfers by Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP to any "successor fund" managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or its Affiliates without the consent of any other Member. Borrower shall cause the Operating Agreement Amendment to eliminate or subordinate such provisions to the restrictions set forth in this Section 10.2, and shall not permit any transfer that would be inconsistent with this Section 10.2, whether or not such transfer is permitted under the Operating Agreement.

### 10.3 No Amendment or Termination of Leases or Material Contracts

Amend, modify, restate, extend, renew, terminate, accept a surrender of or waive any material right under (a) any Lease, except renewals or extensions that do not require Lender's consent under Section 9.6 and that are on market terms, or (b) the Construction Contract, the plans and specifications, the Renovation Budget or any other material contract relating to the Property, except as permitted by Section 7.6.

### 10.4 No Dissolution, Merger or Change of Business

Dissolve, liquidate, wind up, merge, consolidate, convert or reorganize, or change the nature of its business or its organizational form or jurisdiction of organization, or amend its articles of organization or Operating Agreement in any manner that would adversely affect Lender, the Property or the Collateral, or that would alter, eliminate or weaken any single-purpose entity, separateness, Independent Manager or bankruptcy-remoteness provision required by Article 14. Borrower shall not amend, modify or waive any provision of the Operating Agreement relating to single-purpose entity status, separateness, the Independent Manager, restrictions on bankruptcy filings, dissolution, merger or transfers without Lender's prior written consent in each instance.

### 10.5 No Bankruptcy Filing Without Independent Manager Consent

Commence any voluntary case or proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any other federal or state bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, reorganization, liquidation or similar law, consent to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian, make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or admit in writing its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, unless such action has been approved in advance by the affirmative vote of the Independent Manager and by Lender. Borrower shall include in its Operating Agreement a provision requiring the unanimous written consent of the Independent Manager and the Managing Member before any such action may be taken.

### 10.6 No Change in Identity or Location

Change its name, its form of organization, its state of organization, its organizational identification number, its Federal Employer Identification Number, its principal place of business, its chief executive office or its registered agent, or take any action that would render any UCC financing statement filed by Lender seriously misleading, without giving Lender at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice and executing such amendments and new financing statements as Lender may require.

### 10.7 No Alterations or Removal of Fixtures

Make any structural alteration to, or demolish or remove any material portion of, the Improvements (other than the renovation in accordance with Article 7), or remove, detach or permit the removal or detachment of any fixture, building system or item of equipment from the Property, except for the replacement thereof with items of equal or greater value and utility that are free of liens and become subject to the lien of this Mortgage.

### 10.8 No Change of Use; No Residential Use

Change the use of the Property from mixed-use retail and office use, or use or permit the use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Bay 1, Tax Map No. 460-12-04-007) for any residential purpose, or apply for, consent to or permit any rezoning, variance, special exception, conditional use approval or change in the zoning of the Property that would permit residential use of the ground floor of Lot 7 or would otherwise adversely affect the Property or Lender's interest.

### 10.9 No Hazardous Materials

Cause or permit any Hazardous Materials to be brought onto, stored, used, generated, treated, released or disposed of at, on, under or from the Property, except for de minimis quantities of customary cleaning supplies and office supplies used in compliance with Environmental Laws, and Hazardous Materials used in the ordinary course of construction in compliance with Section 10.10.

### 10.10 Construction Materials

Bring onto the Property, use in the renovation or store at the Property any Hazardous Materials (including without limitation solvents, adhesives, sealants, refrigerant and fuel) except in compliance with all Environmental Laws, in quantities customary for the work being performed, and with all required notifications, permits and disposal arrangements.

### 10.11 No Partition or Joint Assessment

Seek or permit any partition of the Property, any subdivision of the Land, or any separate assessment of any portion of the Property, without Lender's prior written consent.

## ARTICLE 11 — INSURANCE

### 11.1 Property Insurance

Borrower shall maintain at all times during the term of the Loan comprehensive all-risk (special form) property insurance covering the Property and all Improvements, on a replacement cost basis, with an agreed amount endorsement (waiver of coinsurance) and without any deductible exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($25,000.00) except for windstorm deductibles not exceeding five percent (5%) of the insured value. Coverage shall include, without limitation, fire, windstorm, hail, explosion, riot, civil commotion, vandalism, malicious mischief, sprinkler leakage, water damage, and such other perils as Lender may reasonably require. Each policy shall name Lender as mortgagee and loss payee pursuant to a standard mortgagee clause, shall be non-contributory and shall provide that Lender's interest shall not be invalidated by any act or neglect of Borrower or any tenant.

### 11.2 Commercial General Liability

Borrower shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with minimum limits of Two Million and No/100 Dollars ($2,000,000.00) per occurrence and Five Million and No/100 Dollars ($5,000,000.00) in the aggregate, naming Lender as an additional insured. Such insurance shall include coverage for premises liability, operations liability, products and completed operations, personal and advertising injury, contractual liability (including the insured contract coverage applicable to the Loan Documents) and, during the Renovation Period, construction and completed operations coverage.

### 11.3 Flood Insurance

Borrower shall maintain flood insurance on the Property in an amount not less than Five Million and No/100 Dollars ($5,000,000.00), naming Lender as mortgagee and loss payee. Borrower acknowledges that (a) the Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X (area of minimal flood hazard) and that federally mandated flood insurance is therefore not required for the Property, and (b) notwithstanding the foregoing, Lender requires flood insurance as an express condition of the Loan, and the failure to maintain such coverage shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 16.1(f) irrespective of any federal flood insurance requirement.

### 11.4 Builder's Risk Insurance

During the Renovation Period, Borrower shall maintain builder's risk insurance (including, at Lender's election, a completed value form or installation floater as appropriate) in an amount not less than the full Renovation Budget of Three Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($3,150,000.00), on a replacement cost basis, covering the Property and the renovation work against all risks of physical loss or damage during the course of construction, including without limitation fire, lightning, windstorm, hail, vandalism, malicious mischief, theft, flood and earthquake (if reasonably required by Lender), and with soft costs, expediting expense and false work coverage reasonably acceptable to Lender. Such insurance shall name Lender as mortgagee and loss payee and shall include a waiver of subrogation in favor of Lender and the Contractor. Upon Substantial Completion, the builder's risk coverage may be terminated, provided that the property insurance required by Section 11.1 is then in full force and effect with respect to the completed renovation.

### 11.5 Workers' Compensation; Umbrella Liability

Borrower shall maintain (a) workers' compensation insurance in the amounts required by the laws of the State of South Carolina, covering all employees of Borrower and, to the extent not covered under the Contractor's policies, all persons engaged in the renovation of the Property, and employer's liability insurance with limits of not less than Five Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($500,000.00), and (b) umbrella or excess liability insurance in an amount not less than Five Million and No/100 Dollars ($5,000,000.00), providing excess coverage over the commercial general liability, automobile liability and employers' liability policies.

### 11.6 General Insurance Requirements

All insurance required under this Article 11 shall (a) be issued by insurers licensed to do business in the State of South Carolina and having an A.M. Best rating of not less than A-:VII or an equivalent rating acceptable to Lender, (b) contain a provision requiring not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Lender of cancellation, non-renewal, reduction in coverage or material modification (and ten (10) days' notice for non-payment of premium), (c) be primary and non-contributory with any insurance maintained by Lender, and (d) be maintained at Borrower's sole cost and expense. Borrower shall deliver to Lender certificates of insurance and, upon request, certified copies of the policies and endorsements, on or before the Closing Date and at least thirty (30) days prior to each policy expiration. If Borrower fails to maintain any required insurance, Lender may (but shall not be obligated to) obtain such insurance and the cost thereof shall constitute an advance under Section 9.14.

### 11.7 Application of Insurance Proceeds

All insurance proceeds shall be applied in accordance with Article 15.

## ARTICLE 12 — ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND LAND USE RESTRICTION

### 12.1 Compliance with Environmental Laws

Borrower shall comply, and shall cause all tenants, contractors, agents and occupants of the Property to comply, with all Environmental Laws, and shall not cause or permit any violation of any Environmental Law, any release of Hazardous Materials or any condition that would reasonably be expected to require remediation, investigation or reporting under any Environmental Law. Borrower shall keep the Property free of any lien imposed under any Environmental Law.

### 12.2 Covenants Regarding the Land Use Restriction

If the DSCR is less than 1.25 to 1.00 as of any DSCR Test Date, Borrower may, within thirty (30) days after the date on which the applicable compliance certificate is due, cure such shortfall by depositing with Lender, in an interest-bearing account controlled by Lender as additional Collateral, an amount equal to the quotient of (a) the shortfall in Net Operating Income required to achieve a DSCR of 1.25 to 1.00 for the applicable period, divided by (b) 0.125. Amounts so deposited shall be released to Borrower upon achievement of a DSCR of not less than 1.25 to 1.00 as of any two (2) consecutive DSCR Test Dates and the absence of any Event of Default, and shall otherwise be applied to the Obligations in accordance with Section 6.5(b). A failure to cure a DSCR shortfall in accordance with this Section 13.5, together with a DSCR of less than 1.25 to 1.00 as of two (2) consecutive DSCR Test Dates, shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 16.1(g).

### 13.6 Interpretation of Financial Covenants

The financial covenants in this Article 13 are intended to measure the performance of the Property and of Borrower based on the definitions set forth herein, and shall be calculated without regard to any inconsistent treatment of Net Operating Income under GAAP. Lender shall not be deemed to have waived any breach of a financial covenant by reason of its acceptance of a compliance certificate or its failure to object to any calculation.

## ARTICLE 14 — SINGLE-PURPOSE ENTITY AND SEPARATENESS

### 14.1 Single-Purpose Entity Status

Borrower shall at all times maintain its status as a single-purpose entity and shall not engage in any business or activity other than the ownership, operation, renovation, leasing, management and disposition of the Property and activities incidental thereto. Borrower's sole purpose, as reflected in its organizational documents, shall be limited to such activities, and Borrower shall not amend its articles of organization or Operating Agreement to broaden such purpose.

### 14.2 Separateness Covenants

Borrower shall at all times:

(a) maintain its own separate books of account, financial records and bank accounts, separate and apart from those of any other Person;

(b) not commingle its funds or assets with those of any Member, Affiliate, manager or other Person;

(c) hold itself out to the public as a legal entity separate and distinct from any other Person, including its Members and Affiliates, and conduct its business in its own name, using its own stationery, invoices and checks;

(d) maintain adequate capitalization in light of its contemplated business operations, transactions and liabilities;

(e) not incur any additional indebtedness, whether secured or unsecured, without Lender's prior written consent;

(f) not guarantee or become obligated for the debts of any other Person, and not hold out its credit as being available to satisfy the obligations of any other Person;

(g) pay its own liabilities and expenses from its own assets and maintain arm's-length relationships with its Members and Affiliates, and enter into transactions with Affiliates only on arm's-length terms;

(h) maintain its assets in such a manner that it is not costly or difficult to segregate, ascertain or identify its individual assets from those of any Member, Affiliate or other Person;

(i) not pledge its assets for the benefit of any other Person, and not make any loans or advances to any Person;

(j) observe all limited liability company formalities and allocate fairly and reasonably any overhead expenses shared with any Affiliate; and

(k) maintain a separate office, or a separately identified portion of a shared office, and a separate telephone number and email address.

### 14.3 Independent Manager

(a) Borrower shall cause its Operating Agreement to require, at all times, the appointment and continuance of an Independent Manager whose affirmative written consent, together with the consent of the Managing Member, shall be required before Borrower may (i) file a voluntary petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any state insolvency, receivership or reorganization law, (ii) consent to or fail to contest in a timely manner any involuntary petition filed against it, (iii) admit in writing its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, (iv) make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, (v) dissolve, liquidate, wind up, merge, consolidate or sell all or substantially all of its assets, or (vi) amend, alter or repeal any single-purpose entity, separateness or bankruptcy-remoteness provision of its organizational documents.

(b) Borrower shall not, and shall cause the Members not to, remove or replace the Independent Manager, or amend the Independent Manager provisions of the Operating Agreement, without Lender's prior written consent.

(c) Borrower shall deliver to Lender, upon request, evidence of the identity and qualifications of the Independent Manager and of the Independent Manager's written consent to serve.

### 14.4 Member Consent Required

Borrower shall cause each Member to execute and deliver the Operating Agreement Amendment and the Members' Consent set forth at the end of this Mortgage, pursuant to which each Member agrees to be bound by the single-purpose entity and separateness restrictions set forth in this Article 14, and agrees that it shall not vote for, consent to or take any action to cause the bankruptcy, insolvency, dissolution, liquidation, merger, consolidation or sale of Borrower or the Property in violation of this Mortgage without Lender's prior written consent and, where applicable, the Independent Manager's consent.

### 14.5 No Amendment of Organizational Documents

Borrower shall not amend, modify, restate, waive or repeal any provision of its articles of organization or Operating Agreement relating to single-purpose entity status, separateness, the Independent Manager, restrictions on transfers, restrictions on bankruptcy filings, dissolution or merger without Lender's prior written consent in each instance, and shall deliver to Lender a copy of any permitted amendment within five (5) Business Days after its execution.

### 14.6 Acknowledgment of Existing Deficiencies

Borrower acknowledges that, as of the date of the redacted summary of the Operating Agreement provided to Lender by Borrower's counsel, the Operating Agreement (a) contained no Independent Manager or independent director provision, (b) contained no separateness covenants and no requirement that Borrower maintain its existence as a single-purpose entity separate and apart from its Members, (c) contained no provision conditioning dissolution, merger or bankruptcy filing upon the consent of any independent party or lender, (d) contained a broad "any lawful business" purpose catch-all in Section 1.4, and (e) did not contain any change-of-control provision addressing upstream or indirect transfers of interests in any Member. Borrower covenants that the Operating Agreement Amendment, executed by Borrower and all Members and delivered as a condition to the initial advance under Section 20.1, cures each such deficiency.

## ARTICLE 15 — CASUALTY AND CONDEMNATION

### 15.1 Notice

Borrower shall give Lender prompt written notice of any casualty affecting the Property or any portion thereof, or of any actual or threatened condemnation, taking or exercise of the power of eminent domain affecting the Property or any portion thereof, together with such information as Lender may reasonably request.

### 15.2 Restoration

If the Property is damaged by casualty or taken by condemnation, Borrower shall, subject to Lender's rights under this Article 15, promptly and diligently repair, restore and rebuild the Property to a condition at least equal to its condition immediately prior to such casualty or taking, in accordance with plans and specifications approved by Lender and in compliance with all applicable laws and the LUR, including the requirements of Section 7.9 with respect to any work affecting the Bay 1 floor slab. Borrower shall obtain and maintain the insurance required by Article 11 and any applicable builder's risk coverage during any restoration.

### 15.3 Application of Proceeds

(a) If the amount of insurance proceeds or condemnation awards, together with all other funds available for restoration, is less than One Million and No/100 Dollars ($1,000,000.00), and no Event of Default exists, such proceeds or awards shall be paid to Borrower and applied to the restoration of the Property, provided that Lender may require that such amounts be held in escrow by Lender and disbursed in accordance with a restoration budget approved by Lender.

(b) If such amount is equal to or greater than $1,000,000.00, or if an Event of Default exists, or if the Property cannot in Lender's reasonable judgment be economically restored, or if the restoration would not be completed at least twelve (12) months prior to the Maturity Date, Lender may elect to apply such proceeds or awards, at its option, (i) to the restoration of the Property in accordance with a budget and disbursement procedure approved by Lender, or (ii) to the payment of the Obligations, whether or not then due, in the order of priority set forth in Section 5.5.

(c) Any application of insurance proceeds or condemnation awards to the Obligations under Section 15.3(b)(ii) shall be made without payment of any prepayment premium, Yield Maintenance Premium or penalty, notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Article 5.

(d) Borrower hereby irrevocably assigns to Lender all insurance proceeds and condemnation awards relating to the Property, and appoints Lender as its attorney-in-fact, coupled with an interest, to endorse any check or draft representing such proceeds or awards and to take all actions necessary to collect, settle and apply the same.

### 15.4 Lender's Right to Apply; Third-Party Interests

Lender may apply any proceeds or awards it receives to any restoration or to the Obligations notwithstanding any objection by Borrower, Guarantor, any tenant or any other Person. No tenant under any Lease shall have any right to any portion of any insurance proceeds or condemnation award except as expressly provided in such Lease and approved in writing by Lender.

## ARTICLE 16 — EVENTS OF DEFAULT

### 16.1 Events of Default

Each of the following shall constitute an "**Event of Default**" under this Mortgage and the other Loan Documents:

(a) **Payment.** Failure by Borrower to make any payment of principal, interest, the Yield Maintenance Premium, a late charge or any other amount due under the Loan Documents when due, subject to the cure period set forth in Section 16.2(a);

(b) **Covenant Default.** Breach by Borrower of any covenant, agreement or obligation contained in this Mortgage or in any other Loan Document (other than a breach described in any other clause of this Section 16.1), continuing beyond the applicable cure period set forth in Section 16.2(b);

(c) **Misrepresentation.** Any representation or warranty made by Borrower or Guarantor in any Loan Document, or in any certificate or report delivered in connection therewith, proving to be materially false, misleading or inaccurate in any material respect when made or deemed made;

(d) **Bankruptcy; Insolvency.** The filing by Borrower or Guarantor of a voluntary petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any state insolvency, receivership or reorganization law, the consent by Borrower or Guarantor to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian for any substantial part of its property or assets, any assignment for the benefit of creditors by Borrower or Guarantor, the admission in writing by Borrower or Guarantor of its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, or the filing of an involuntary petition against Borrower or Guarantor that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian for any substantial part of the property or assets of Borrower or Guarantor that is not discharged within sixty (60) days;

(e) **Cross-Default.** A default by Borrower or Guarantor under any other indebtedness for borrowed money in an amount exceeding Two Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($250,000.00), individually or in the aggregate, which default is not cured within any applicable cure or grace period, or the acceleration of any such indebtedness;

(f) **Insurance.** Failure by Borrower to maintain any insurance required under Article 11 or to deliver the certificates and endorsements required by Section 11.6, subject to the cure period set forth in Section 16.2(d);

(g) **DSCR.** The DSCR being less than 1.25 to 1.00 as of two (2) consecutive DSCR Test Dates, without cure in accordance with Section 13.5;

(h) **Reserves.** Failure by Borrower to make any deposit into any Reserve Account when required, or failure to replenish the Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve Account within thirty (30) days after Lender's written demand in accordance with Section 6.3, or failure to make any deposit into the Capital Replacement Reserve Account or the Tax and Insurance Escrow Account;

(i) **Single-Purpose Entity.** Breach of any covenant set forth in Article 14, including any failure to maintain an Independent Manager or any amendment to the Operating Agreement that eliminates or weakens any single-purpose entity, separateness or bankruptcy-remoteness provision;

(j) **Substantial Completion.** Failure by Borrower to achieve Substantial Completion of the renovation on or before the Substantial Completion Deadline, subject to Section 16.2(e);

(k) **Transfer Restrictions.** Any sale, transfer, encumbrance, pledge or other disposition of the Property or of any direct or indirect interest in Borrower in violation of Section 10.2, or any change of control of Borrower or of a Controlling Member without Lender's prior written consent;

(l) **Land Use Restriction; Environmental.** Any failure by Borrower to comply with the LUR or with any covenant set forth in Article 12, including without limitation any use of the ground floor of Lot 7 for residential purposes, any penetration, removal or compromise of the vapor barrier beneath the Bay 1 floor slab without SCDHEC approval and Lender consent, any failure to conduct or deliver the vapor barrier inspections required by Section 12.2(c), or any modification, termination or vacation of the LUR without Lender's consent;

(m) **Material Adverse Effect.** The occurrence of a Material Adverse Effect that, in Lender's reasonable judgment, materially impairs the ability of Borrower to perform its obligations under the Loan Documents or of Guarantor to perform its obligations under the Guaranty, the Completion Guaranty or the Payment Guaranty;

(n) **Guaranty.** A default by Guarantor under the Guaranty, the Completion Guaranty, the Payment Guaranty or the Environmental Indemnity, or any attempt by Guarantor to revoke, terminate, disavow or limit its liability thereunder;

(o) **Abandonment.** The abandonment of the Property, the cessation of operations at the Property for more than thirty (30) consecutive days (other than as a result of a casualty or condemnation being diligently restored), or the removal from the Property of a material portion of the Collateral;

(p) **Other Loan Documents.** The occurrence of any other event or condition that constitutes an Event of Default under any other Loan Document; or

(q) **Invalidity.** Any Loan Document ceasing to be in full force and effect, or any party thereto asserting that any Loan Document is not a valid and binding obligation of such party, or any lien granted under this Mortgage ceasing to be a valid first-priority lien on the Property (subject only to the Permitted Exceptions).

### 16.2 Notice and Cure Periods

The following cure periods shall apply to the Events of Default described in Section 16.1:

(a) **Payment Defaults.** Five (5) Business Days after the date on which payment was due.

(b) **Non-Monetary Defaults.** Thirty (30) calendar days after written notice from Lender to Borrower of the default; provided, however, that if the default is of a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) calendar days and Borrower has commenced and is diligently pursuing the cure thereof, the cure period shall be extended for an additional period not to exceed sixty (60) calendar days (for a total cure period not to exceed ninety (90) calendar days). No such notice or cure period shall apply to any default that consists of a failure to pay money or to any Event of Default described in Section 16.2(c), (d) or (e).

(c) **Single-Purpose Entity, Transfer and Bankruptcy Defaults.** No cure period. Any breach of the covenants set forth in Article 14 or Section 10.2, and any event described in Section 16.1(d), shall constitute an immediate Event of Default without notice or opportunity to cure.

(d) **Insurance Defaults.** Five (5) Business Days after written notice from Lender to Borrower; provided that if the applicable policy has lapsed, Lender may obtain such insurance in accordance with Section 11.6 without further notice and the cost thereof shall constitute an advance under Section 9.14.

(e) **Substantial Completion Defaults.** No cure period; provided, however, that Lender may, in its reasonable discretion and upon Borrower's written request delivered before the Substantial Completion Deadline, extend the Substantial Completion Deadline by up to sixty (60) days in the aggregate on account of delays caused by events beyond Borrower's reasonable control (including casualty, governmental delay in the issuance of permits or certificates of occupancy, and labor disputes) that are not caused by any act, omission or breach of Borrower, Guarantor or the Contractor.

### 16.3 Lender's Right to Cure

Lender may, but shall have no obligation to, cure any default of Borrower under the Loan Documents. Any amounts expended by Lender in doing so shall constitute advances under Section 9.14, shall bear interest at the Default Rate and shall be secured by this Mortgage. Lender's exercise of this right shall not cure any Event of Default or waive any of Lender's rights.

### 16.4 Notice of Default as to Tenants

Borrower acknowledges that Lender may, following the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, deliver the notices to tenants contemplated by Section 3.3, and that such notices shall be effective upon delivery in accordance with the applicable Lease and Section 21.1.

## ARTICLE 17 — REMEDIES

### 17.1 Judicial Foreclosure; No Power of Sale

Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender may, in addition to all other rights and remedies available to it, foreclose this Mortgage in accordance with the laws of the State of South Carolina. Borrower acknowledges and agrees that the State of South Carolina is a judicial foreclosure jurisdiction and that this Mortgage does not, and shall not be construed to, grant Lender any power of sale, any right to sell the Property without judicial proceedings, or any other remedy not available to a mortgagee under the laws of the State of South Carolina. Any provision of this Mortgage that might be construed to grant a power of sale shall be deemed deleted and of no force or effect. Lender may also proceed to enforce the Note by an action at law for the indebtedness secured hereby, or may pursue any other remedy available to it, and may pursue such remedies concurrently or successively, in such order as Lender may elect, subject only to applicable law.

### 17.2 Receiver

Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender shall be entitled, without notice and without regard to the adequacy of any security for the Obligations, to the appointment of a receiver for the Property in any judicial proceeding to enforce this Mortgage, and Borrower consents to such appointment and agrees not to contest the same. Any receiver appointed shall have all powers and duties conferred by applicable law and by the order of appointment, including the power to manage the Property, collect the Rents, make repairs, and apply the net proceeds thereof as the court directs.

### 17.3 Remedies Under the UCC

Lender shall have all rights and remedies of a secured party under the UCC with respect to the Personal Property Collateral, including the rights set forth in Part 6 of Article 9 of the UCC, in addition to the rights and remedies provided in this Mortgage. Borrower agrees that ten (10) days' prior written notice of the time and place of any public sale or of the time after which any private sale or other disposition is to be made shall be commercially reasonable, and that any disposition of the Personal Property Collateral may be conducted on the Property. Lender may require Borrower to assemble the Personal Property Collateral and make it available to Lender at a place reasonably convenient to Lender.

### 17.4 Collection of Rents Following Default

Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender may exercise all rights under Article 3, including the right to collect the Rents directly, to notify tenants, and to enforce the Leases, in each case without the necessity of obtaining a court order, appointing a receiver or taking any other action, and the license granted to Borrower under Section 3.2 shall be automatically revoked.

### 17.5 Entry and Performance

Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender may enter upon and take possession of the Property, without notice, to perform any obligation of Borrower under the Loan Documents, to protect or preserve the Collateral, to make repairs and to complete the renovation, and may exclude Borrower, its agents and employees from the Property to the extent necessary to do so. Borrower authorizes Lender to take such actions and shall cooperate fully.

### 17.6 Application of Proceeds

The proceeds of any foreclosure sale, any collection of Rents, any sale of Personal Property Collateral and any other amounts received by Lender after an Event of Default shall be applied in the order of priority set forth in Section 5.5, and any surplus shall be paid to Borrower or to such other Person as may be entitled thereto by law.

### 17.7 Deficiency

If the proceeds of any foreclosure sale and the application of all other Collateral are insufficient to pay the Obligations in full, Lender may seek a deficiency judgment against Borrower and, to the extent provided in Article 18, against Guarantor, in accordance with applicable law. Nothing in this Section 17.7 shall limit or impair the obligations of Guarantor under the Guaranty, the Completion Guaranty, the Payment Guaranty or the Environmental Indemnity.

### 17.8 Cumulative Remedies; No Waiver

No right or remedy of Lender under the Loan Documents or applicable law is exclusive of any other right or remedy, and each shall be cumulative and in addition to every other right and remedy. No failure or delay by Lender in exercising any right, power or remedy shall operate as a waiver thereof, and no single or partial exercise shall preclude any other or further exercise. Any waiver by Lender shall be effective only if in writing and only to the extent expressly stated therein.

### 17.9 Waiver of Certain Rights; Non-Waivable Rights

To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, Borrower waives (a) any right to a marshalling of assets or a sale in inverse order of alienation, (b) any appraisal, valuation, stay, extension, homestead, exemption or moratorium law now or hereafter in force, (c) any right to require Lender to proceed against any other Person or any other security before proceeding against the Property or Borrower, and (d) any notice of the occurrence of an Event of Default, of acceleration, of intent to foreclose, or of the time, place and terms of sale, except as expressly required by the Loan Documents or by applicable law that cannot be waived. Nothing in this Mortgage waives any right of Borrower or Guarantor that is non-waivable under applicable law, including any non-waivable statutory right or any right to notice required by applicable law.

### 17.10 Attorneys' Fees and Enforcement Costs

Borrower shall pay all costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees and disbursements, court costs, receiver's fees, appraisal fees, title search and title insurance charges, publication costs and trustee or commissioner fees, incurred by Lender in connection with the enforcement of the Loan Documents, the foreclosure of this Mortgage, the collection of the Obligations, any workout, forbearance, bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding, or the protection or preservation of the Collateral. If Lender is made a party to any litigation or proceeding affecting the Property or the Loan, Borrower shall pay all costs and reasonable attorneys' fees incurred by Lender in connection therewith. All such amounts shall be secured by this Mortgage and shall bear interest at the Default Rate from the date of demand.

### 17.11 No Impairment of Security

Lender's acceptance of any payment after the due date, its failure to accelerate the Loan upon any Event of Default, its acceptance of a deed in lieu of foreclosure, its release of any portion of the Collateral, its modification of any Loan Document, its extension of the Maturity Date, or any other act or omission of Lender shall not release, impair or otherwise affect the lien of this Mortgage, the Assignment of Leases and Rents or the obligations of Borrower or Guarantor, except to the extent expressly provided in a written instrument executed by Lender.

## ARTICLE 18 — NON-RECOURSE AND RECOURSE CARVE-OUTS

### 18.1 Non-Recourse Obligations

Except as expressly provided in this Article 18, in the Environmental Indemnity and in any other Loan Document, no Member, manager, officer, employee or Affiliate of Borrower shall have any personal liability for the payment or performance of the Obligations, and Lender's recourse shall be limited to the Property and the other Collateral and to the obligations of Guarantor under the Guaranty, the Completion Guaranty and the Payment Guaranty. Borrower acknowledges that the Loan is structured as a non-recourse loan subject to the carve-outs set forth in Section 18.2, and that the Guaranty, the Completion Guaranty and the Payment Guaranty are separate obligations that are not limited by this Section 18.1.

### 18.2 Recourse Carve-Out Events

Notwithstanding Section 18.1, and in addition to all other obligations of Guarantor, the Obligations shall become fully recourse to Borrower and to Guarantor, jointly and severally, for the entire outstanding amount of the Obligations (and not merely the portion attributable to the loss or damage caused), upon the occurrence of any of the following (each, a "**Carve-Out Event**"):

(a) fraud or intentional misrepresentation by Borrower, Guarantor or any of their respective agents, officers, members or employees in connection with the Loan or any Loan Document, including without limitation any material misrepresentation in any rent roll, estoppel certificate, financial statement or certification delivered to Lender;

(b) the misapplication or misappropriation of (i) any Rents, including security deposits, (ii) any insurance proceeds or condemnation awards, (iii) any tenant improvement or leasing commission funds, or (iv) any Reserve Account funds, in each case by Borrower, Guarantor or any of their respective agents;

(c) the filing of a voluntary petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any state insolvency, reorganization, receivership or similar law by or on behalf of Borrower, or the consent by Borrower to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian, or Borrower's admission in writing of its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, or Borrower's making of an assignment for the benefit of creditors;

(d) environmental liability arising from the acts or omissions of Borrower, Guarantor or their respective agents, including without limitation any breach of Article 12, any violation of the LUR, any penetration, removal or compromise of the vapor barrier beneath the Bay 1 floor slab, or any failure to comply with an order of SCDHEC, in each case to the extent of all losses, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees and consultants' fees) incurred by Lender as a result; and

(e) any violation of the transfer restrictions set forth in Section 10.2.

### 18.3 Relationship to Guaranties

The recourse provided under Section 18.2 is in addition to, and not in limitation of, (a) the obligations of Guarantor under the Guaranty (which shall be a full recourse guaranty of the Obligations to the extent provided therein), (b) the obligations of Guarantor under the Completion Guaranty and the Payment Guaranty, and (c) the obligations of Borrower and Guarantor under the Environmental Indemnity, which shall not be limited by this Article 18 in any respect. No exercise or non-exercise of rights under this Article 18 shall impair, limit or release any obligation under any guaranty or the Environmental Indemnity.

### 18.4 Recourse for Lender's Costs

Notwithstanding Section 18.1, Borrower shall in all events be personally liable for (a) all amounts payable under Section 17.10, (b) all advances made by Lender under Section 9.14, (c) all amounts owed with respect to any Reserve Account, and (d) all interest, late charges and other amounts accruing on the foregoing.

## ARTICLE 19 — OTHER LOAN DOCUMENTS

### 19.1 Guaranty; Completion Guaranty; Payment Guaranty

Borrower acknowledges that Guarantor has executed and delivered to Lender (a) the Guaranty, (b) the Completion Guaranty, unconditionally guaranteeing the completion of the renovation described in Article 7 within the Renovation Budget and by the Substantial Completion Deadline, and (c) the Payment Guaranty, guaranteeing payment of any shortfall in debt service payments during the first fourteen (14) months following the Closing Date to the extent that Net Operating Income from the Property is insufficient to cover monthly interest payments during such period. Borrower shall cause Guarantor to perform all of its obligations under each such instrument.

### 19.2 Environmental Indemnity

Borrower and Guarantor have executed and delivered the Environmental Indemnity, which shall be an independent obligation and shall survive as provided in Section 12.4 and therein.

### 19.3 Financing Statements and Filings

Borrower shall, at its sole cost, execute and deliver (a) a UCC-1 financing statement naming Borrower, as debtor, and Lender, as secured party, to be filed with the South Carolina Secretary of State, covering all Personal Property Collateral, (b) a fixture filing to be recorded in the RMC Office, and (c) all continuation statements, amendments and additional filings necessary to maintain perfection. Borrower acknowledges that the description of collateral in such filings shall be consistent with the description in this Mortgage.

### 19.4 Operating Agreement Amendment; Members' Consent

Borrower shall cause the Operating Agreement Amendment and the Members' Consent to be executed and delivered to Lender on or before the Closing Date, and shall cause each Member to comply therewith at all times during the term of the Loan.

### 19.5 Cross-Default

Any Event of Default under this Mortgage shall constitute a default under the Note and each other Loan Document, and any default under the Note, the Guaranty, the Completion Guaranty, the Payment Guaranty or the Environmental Indemnity shall constitute an Event of Default under this Mortgage.

### 19.6 No Impairment of Guaranties

Lender may, without notice to or consent of Borrower or Guarantor and without impairing or releasing the obligations of Guarantor, (a) extend or renew the Loan or the Maturity Date, (b) modify, amend or supplement any Loan Document, (c) release or subordinate any Collateral, (d) grant any indulgence or forbearance, and (e) settle, compromise or release any claim against any Person. Borrower irrevocably consents to the foregoing to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.

### 19.7 Conflicts Among Loan Documents

In the event of any conflict or inconsistency among the Loan Documents, (a) the Note shall control as to the principal amount of the Loan, the Interest Rate, the payment dates, the Maturity Date, the prepayment terms and other payment terms, (b) this Mortgage shall control as to the description and scope of the Collateral, the creation, perfection and enforcement of liens and security interests, and the rights and remedies of Lender with respect to the Property, and (c) the Environmental Indemnity shall control as to the allocation of environmental liability. In the event of any conflict between the Term Sheet and any Loan Document, the Loan Documents shall control, in accordance with Section 14.3 of the Term Sheet; provided that no Loan Document shall be deemed to amend or supersede the Term Sheet except as expressly set forth therein.

## ARTICLE 20 — CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO ADVANCES

### 20.1 Conditions to the Initial Advance

Lender's obligation to make the initial advance of the Loan is subject to the satisfaction, in form and substance satisfactory to Lender and its counsel, of each of the following conditions precedent:

(a) execution and delivery of all Loan Documents, including the Note, this Mortgage, the Guaranty, the Completion Guaranty, the Payment Guaranty, the Environmental Indemnity and the UCC-1 financing statements;

(b) recording of the deed from Hampstead Village Holdings LLC to Borrower and of this Mortgage in the RMC Office, in form satisfactory to Lender and the title insurer, with the deed and this Mortgage to be recorded concurrently;

(c) receipt by Lender of the Title Policy (or a pro forma policy or irrevocable commitment to issue the Title Policy) from Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc. through Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178), in the amount of $14,750,000.00, insuring the first-priority lien of this Mortgage subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, together with such endorsements as Lender may reasonably require, including without limitation zoning, access, survey, comprehensive, future advance, contiguity (if available) and such endorsements as may be available with respect to the Anson Lane strip and the balcony encroachment;

(d) receipt by Lender of a current ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey of the Property conforming to the 2021 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements, prepared by a surveyor licensed in the State of South Carolina, certified to Lender, the title insurer and Borrower, dated or re-certified not more than ninety (90) days prior to the Closing Date, and showing all improvements, encroachments, easements and rights-of-way described in Exhibit B;

(e) receipt by Lender of a gap indemnity and such owner's affidavits, lien waivers and other instruments as the title insurer may require to delete the standard exceptions from the Title Policy;

(f) receipt by Lender of the Phase I Report and evidence that Lender is an intended user thereof and that Borrower has obtained the reliance rights of an intended user;

No condition precedent under this Article 20 may be waived except by a written instrument executed by Lender expressly identifying the condition waived and stating that it is waived. Lender's failure to insist upon strict satisfaction of any condition precedent shall not constitute a waiver of such condition with respect to any subsequent advance.
